projectorSlides.title: Le tournant de l’IA en marketing
projectorSlides.script: Hi, and welcome to the course! I'm thrilled to be your host, as we journey through the world of AI in marketing.
projectorSlides.technology: un assistant IA génératif de votre choix

projectorSlides.title: La puissance de l’IA en marketing
projectorSlides.script:
What if you could brainstorm 50 ad copy variations in 30 seconds? Or build a strong first draft for a distribution plan for your next campaign before your coffee gets cold? Or analyze your campaign's performance and present it to your CMO without writing one line of code?

That's the power of AI in marketing, and by the end of this course, you'll know exactly how to make it happen.

projectorSlides.title: À la fin de ce cours
projectorSlides.script:
You'll learn to leverage AI to supercharge every stage of your marketing workflow, from research and planning all the way through to measurement and iteration. 

You'll also gain a mental model for when AI is useful for marketing workflows, and how to best communicate with AI systems.

projectorSlides.title: Ce que couvre ce cours
projectorSlides.script:
This course is practical, so instead of getting bogged down in theory, we'll be focusing on applied use-cases of AI in marketing. 

We'll primarily use the chat interface of un assistant IA génératif de votre choix for our examples and exercises, but here's the great news: The principles of communication with AI and the marketing workflows we cover are universal.

projectorSlides.title: Ce que couvre ce cours
projectorSlides.script:
So everything you learn applies to other AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or even private LLMs your organizations may use.

With that said, let's get started.

projectorSlides.title: IA et marketing : un duo idéal
projectorSlides.script:
AI and marketing are truly a match made in heaven. Marketing workflows are inherently “Generative”.

Content marketers can build article outlines, improve the SEO potential of blogs, and build useful first drafts for their content.

projectorSlides.title: IA et marketing : un duo idéal
projectorSlides.script: Social Media teams can use generative AI to generate or refine social copy.

projectorSlides.title: IA et marketing : un duo idéal
projectorSlides.script:
Product marketers can ideate website tag lines or even create prototypes of landing pages to better collaborate with design.

And a host of other use-cases that all types of marketing teams can leverage.

projectorSlides.title: Le cycle de vie marketing
projectorSlides.script:
And while every team within the marketing function works on different projects, AI can be useful across the entirety of the marketing life cycle.

Be that with research, planning, and ideation, where projects are scoped, campaigns are planned, and goals are set. 

Creation and execution, when creative assets are created.  

Measurement and optimization, where outcomes are tracked, and execution is refined based on the data.

And finally, iteration and scaling, where marketers double down on what works and expand successful tactics for new campaigns.

projectorSlides.title: Cadrer des campagnes marketing avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script: Welcome back! So far, we've explored the marketing lifecycle and saw how campaigns move through distinct phases from research to scaling.
projectorSlides.technology: un assistant IA génératif de votre choix

projectorSlides.title: Recherche, planification et idéation
projectorSlides.script: Now, we'll learn how AI can accelerate the most critical phase: research, planning, and ideation, and how it can enable good marketers, to become great ones.

projectorSlides.title: Distribution > création
projectorSlides.script:
In marketing, distribution is king. 

The reason is simple, even if you have the best product, the most interesting white paper, or the most thought provoking blog post, these assets will not have an impact, without strong distribution.

projectorSlides.title: Bons marketeurs vs excellents marketeurs
projectorSlides.script: At the start of any project, good marketers will gravitate towards perfecting assets like landing pages, conference tracks, or content.

projectorSlides.title: Bons marketeurs vs excellents marketeurs
projectorSlides.script: Whereas great marketers will invest time upfront in thorough planning, understanding their audience, mapping distribution channels, and defining success metrics before any creation starts.

projectorSlides.title: Recherche et planification avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script: AI can compress weeks of research and planning into hours, allowing us to level up from good marketers, to great marketers. Let’s showcase this with an example.

projectorSlides.title: Planifier des campagnes avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script: Imagine you're building a marketing campaign for a new fitness app launch. You have limited budget, multiple potential channels to consider, and stakeholders expecting a strong plan.

projectorSlides.title: Planifier des campagnes avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script: Instead of starting with a blank document and hours of research, we can use AI to accelerate it.

projectorSlides.title: Objectifs, contexte et limites
projectorSlides.script: What's important to consider, is that AI is only as good as the information we provide. To get valuable insights, we need to communicate three critical elements clearly: our goals, our context, and our limitations.

projectorSlides.title: Définir des objectifs clairs
projectorSlides.script:
First, we need to define our goals. In this case, we can say our goal is to build a marketing campaign that will generate 10,000 app downloads within 30 days. 

A good goal is clear and has clearly defined, measurable outcomes. A bad goal is vague, and leaves much room for interpretation.
projectorSlides.content:
$$ 
> _Créez une campagne marketing pour la nouvelle app de suivi fitness {x} afin de générer 10 000 téléchargements en 30 jours._

**À quoi ressemblent de bons objectifs** 
- Formulés clairement 
- Résultats bien définis 
- Mesurables si pertinent 

$$

**À quoi ressemblent de mauvais objectifs** 
- Vagues et flous 
- Sans résultats définis
projectorSlides.contentLeft:
$$ 
> _Créez une campagne marketing pour la nouvelle app de suivi fitness {x} afin de générer 10 000 téléchargements en 30 jours._
projectorSlides.contentRight:
**À quoi ressemblent de bons objectifs** 
- Formulés clairement 
- Résultats bien définis 
- Mesurables si pertinent 

$$

**À quoi ressemblent de mauvais objectifs** 
- Vagues et flous 
- Sans résultats définis

projectorSlides.title: Fournir le contexte
projectorSlides.script:
Now, we provide context. Consider this any information that would be useful in defining your campaign. In this example, this is information about our audience, our application, total channels available such as social media, paid advertising, app store optimization, and partnerships. It also includes our total budget. 

Good context provides clear information the AI needs to fulfill its task. A good mental model here, is what context would you provide a new colleague if you wanted them to build a plan?

Conversely, bad context is vague, it does not provide adequate information, and omits key information.
projectorSlides.content:
> _Notre cible est les passionnés de fitness. L’app est disponible sur iOS et Android. Canaux : réseaux sociaux (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook), email marketing, content marketing, publicité payante (Google Ads, Meta Ads), ASO et partenariats. Budget total : 15 000 $._

**À quoi ressemble un bon contexte** 
- Toutes les infos utiles pour accomplir la tâche 
- En marketing : audiences, budget, canaux, etc. 

$$

**À quoi ressemble un mauvais contexte**

1. Cadrer des campagnes marketing avec l’IA
Welcome back! So far, we've explored the marketing lifecycle and saw how campaigns move through distinct phases from research to scaling.

2. Recherche, planification et idéation
Now, we'll learn how AI can accelerate the most critical phase: research, planning, and ideation, and how it can enable good marketers, to become great ones.

3. Distribution > création
In marketing, distribution is king. 

The reason is simple, even if you have the best product, the most interesting white paper, or the most thought provoking blog post, these assets will not have an impact, without strong distribution.

4. Bons marketeurs vs excellents marketeurs
At the start of any project, good marketers will gravitate towards perfecting assets like landing pages, conference tracks, or content.

5. Bons marketeurs vs excellents marketeurs
Whereas great marketers will invest time upfront in thorough planning, understanding their audience, mapping distribution channels, and defining success metrics before any creation starts.

6. Recherche et planification avec l’IA
AI can compress weeks of research and planning into hours, allowing us to level up from good marketers, to great marketers. Let’s showcase this with an example.

7. Planifier des campagnes avec l’IA
Imagine you're building a marketing campaign for a new fitness app launch. You have limited budget, multiple potential channels to consider, and stakeholders expecting a strong plan.

8. Planifier des campagnes avec l’IA
Instead of starting with a blank document and hours of research, we can use AI to accelerate it.

9. Objectifs, contexte et limites
What's important to consider, is that AI is only as good as the information we provide. To get valuable insights, we need to communicate three critical elements clearly: our goals, our context, and our limitations.

10. Définir des objectifs clairs
First, we need to define our goals. In this case, we can say our goal is to build a marketing campaign that will generate 10,000 app downloads within 30 days. 

A good goal is clear and has clearly defined, measurable outcomes. A bad goal is vague, and leaves much room for interpretation.

11. Fournir le contexte
Now, we provide context. Consider this any information that would be useful in defining your campaign. In this example, this is information about our audience, our application, total channels available such as social media, paid advertising, app store optimization, and partnerships. It also includes our total budget. 

Good context provides clear information the AI needs to fulfill its task. A good mental model here, is what context would you provide a new colleague if you wanted them to build a plan?

Conversely, bad context is vague, it does not provide adequate information, and omits key information.

12. Ajouter des limites
Next up, are limitations. 

In this example, we specify the size of our email list, the budget dedicated to paid ads, and our production capacity for blog posts and social. We also mention that we cannot use influencer partnerships as a distribution channel.  

Good limitations provide the constraints our AI needs to be aware of. Bad limitations do not properly address your actual constraints.

13. Notre prompt final
Our final prompt is here, and we're ready to send it off.

14. Rédaction en cours
Once it's sent off, we wait on the output.

15. Réduire la planification de semaines à heures
And voila, we have a strong first draft for a campaign. As always though, make sure to review and scrutinize what AI systems are providing in terms of output, and iterate based on the specifics of your team, and organization.

16. Passons à la pratique !
Now, let's scope our marketing campaigns with AI.

In this video, we'll focus on how AI can be an ideation partner as we execute on these initiatives.

projectorSlides.title: IA pour l’idéation
projectorSlides.script:
A common misconception is that AI can only help in execution for marketing workflows. 

However, AI can also help marketers think outside of the box and see beyond tried and tested playbooks, offering fresh perspectives and unconventional approaches that could help campaigns cut through the noise.

projectorSlides.title: IA pour l’idéation
projectorSlides.script: For example, you can prompt AI tools to challenge assumptions, synthesize trends, critique your plans, propose new channels to explore, and more.

projectorSlides.title: IA pour l’idéation
projectorSlides.script:
Moreover, AI can be useful for ideation within the flow of everyday tasks. It can help generate tactical ideas as you work. 

If you're a growth marketer, you can find relevant subreddits or online communities for outreach. 

If you're a content marketer, you can quickly research compelling statistics to strengthen your articles. 

If you're managing social media, you can generate diverse content angles to keep your feed fresh. 

If you're building partnerships, you can identify prospect partners to target.

This embedded ideation helps marketers move faster while being exhaustive.

In this video, we'll focus on how AI can be an ideation partner as we execute on these initiatives.

transcriptSegments.heading: 2. IA pour l’idéation
transcriptSegments.text:
A common misconception is that AI can only help in execution for marketing workflows. 

However, AI can also help marketers think outside of the box and see beyond tried and tested playbooks, offering fresh perspectives and unconventional approaches that could help campaigns cut through the noise.

transcriptSegments.heading: 3. IA pour l’idéation
transcriptSegments.text: For example, you can prompt AI tools to challenge assumptions, synthesize trends, critique your plans, propose new channels to explore, and more.

transcriptSegments.heading: 4. IA pour l’idéation
transcriptSegments.text:
Moreover, AI can be useful for ideation within the flow of everyday tasks. It can help generate tactical ideas as you work. 

If you're a growth marketer, you can find relevant subreddits or online communities for outreach. 

If you're a content marketer, you can quickly research compelling statistics to strengthen your articles. 

If you're managing social media, you can generate diverse content angles to keep your feed fresh. 

If you're building partnerships, you can identify prospect partners to target.

This embedded ideation helps marketers move faster while being exhaustive.

transcriptSegments.heading: 5. Recherche approfondie : une des killer apps de l’IA
transcriptSegments.text: This ideation is powered by deep research—one of the true superpowers of generative AI systems. By combining the intelligence of large language models with live internet access, these systems can quickly summarize and synthesize insights for a given research task.

transcriptSegments.heading: 6. La recherche approfondie est une fonctionnalité commune à tous les outils d’IA
transcriptSegments.text: In this course, we’ll use the l’assistant IA choisi Researcher agent to illustrate Deep Research workflows.

transcriptSegments.heading: 7. La recherche approfondie est une fonctionnalité commune à tous les outils d’IA
transcriptSegments.text: Just know, that all of your favorite GenAI tools have this functionality.

transcriptSegments.heading: 8. Recherche approfondie dans l’assistant IA choisi
transcriptSegments.text: To access the Researcher Agent in l’assistant IA choisi, simply go to the agents tab, and press on the researcher agent. The Researcher Agent will be able to develop a synthesized brief based on the requirements of your prompt. Let's put it to the test.

transcriptSegments.heading: 9. Idéer des pages de concours avec l’IA
transcriptSegments.text: Imagine you're a growth marketer at SleepWell, a consumer tech company selling a smart sleep tracking mattress.

transcriptSegments.heading: 10. Idéer des pages de concours avec l’IA
transcriptSegments.text:
Our plan is to create competition pages such as “SleepWell vs [Competitor]”, hoping to drive more conversions with these pages from prospects in North America. 

To get an exhaustive list, we perform deep research using l’assistant IA choisi.

transcriptSegments.heading: 11. Définir l’objectif
transcriptSegments.text:
We navigate to the researcher agent, and we start prompting. The same communication principles of goal, context, and limitations, apply here. 

We start with our goal, to create an exhaustive list of top mattress providers ranked by market share and size.

transcriptSegments.heading: 12. Ajouter du contexte
transcriptSegments.text: We then add your context, that the mattress providers need to be segmented by both smart mattresses, and normal mattresses, and that we would like to compare all of their features in a table for easy consumption.

transcriptSegments.heading: 13. Ajouter des contraintes
transcriptSegments.text: Next up, we add our limitations, which is to only focus on the North America market.

transcriptSegments.heading: 14. Recherche approfondie en cours
transcriptSegments.text: l’assistant IA choisi then starts the deep research process. This can take up to 10 to 15 minutes.

transcriptSegments.heading: 15. Rapports détaillés en quelques minutes
transcriptSegments.text: And voila, we get a detailed report.

transcriptSegments.heading: 16. Passons à la pratique !
transcriptSegments.text: Now, let's put your AI research skills to the test.

projectorSlides.title: Règle 1 : Parlez la langue de votre audience
projectorSlides.script: The first rule for creating quality content with AI is to leverage your research and ideation to speak the language of the customer. This is where AI research pays off.

projectorSlides.title: Règle 1 : Parlez la langue de votre audience
projectorSlides.script: Effective research for content creation comes in the form of understanding your audience's pain points, getting strong statistics that back up your claims, and building an outline that speaks to the challenges of your target persona.

projectorSlides.title: Règle 1 : Parlez la langue de votre audience

For example, if you're writing a blog post about the "best running shoes for beginners," effective research may uncover the following: The exact questions beginners ask in running forums (like "how much should I spend?" or "do I need special insoles?"), the language your audience uses when thinking about their running shoes, common pain points that trip up new runners, and useful stats that could strenthen your content. 

Using this context in your prompts helps you create a blog post that answers real questions and fills content gaps, rather than generic listicles that blend in with every other article on Google.

projectorSlides.script:
AI image generation fits in many marketing workflows.

Whether rapid prototyping when submitting design requests, low-stakes content assets like blog headers, or even paid media and organic social posts where we need fresh creative constantly.

projectorSlides.title: Bonnes pratiques pour créer des images avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script:
Creating effective AI imagery follows similar principles to AI communication, goals, context, and limitations are everything. 

On the goals side, we need to be explicit about what we're creating. What's the objective of the image? What should the image include? What's the aspect ratio? 

On the context side, we need to provide your AI tool with all the context it needs to create on-brand high quality imagery. 

This can be uploading our logo, specifying exact hex codes for our brand color scheme, defining our typography preferences, sharing reference images of our desired style, and even the moods it should evoke. The more context you provide, the more on-brand your results will be. 

Think of it like briefing a designer—the more specific we are, the better the output.

On limitations, think of any constraints it needs to be aware of. For example, to not include certain icons, or any other other elements we should omit.

**Définir des objectifs clairs**
- _« Créez une image pour l’en-tête d’un article de blog sur les meilleures chaussures de running en 2026… »_
- _« Créez une image 16:9 d’un flacon de parfum sur une table… »_

**Définir un contexte clair**
- _« Utilisez le logo de l’entreprise joint »_
- _« Utilisez les couleurs #00FFFF, #FF00FF, #00FF00, et la police Roboto »_
- _« L’image doit évoquer une ambiance futuriste »_

**Définir des limites claires**
- _« N’incluez pas l’icône {x} dans l’image »_

projectorSlides.script:
Let's take an example that's close to home, and try to create an image that advertises this course you're taking right now. We'll use l’assistant IA choisi here, but you can try this out in any AI system that supports image generation.

First on the goal. We want to create a 16:9 image that promotes the Neopolis Akademy course "AI for Marketing".

On context, we want the image to include the Neopolis Akademy logo, the Neopolis Akademy font which is Poppins, and the Neopolis Akademy color palette featuring Neon Green, Navy Blue, and White. The hex codes for these colors are added on screen. 

Then, we want include the tag line "Accelerate your marketing workflows with AI". We need to include subtle design elements that evoke AI and technology.

Finally, we want the image to not include any icons related to marketing workflows, as I want only icons generated to evoke data and AI.

projectorSlides.script: Not bad right? We can easily use this to ideate with our design team on what the final product should look like.

projectorSlides.title: Comprendre les limites
projectorSlides.script:
Now for the reality check. AI image generation is powerful, but it's not perfect yet. You'll encounter limitations that are important to understand. 

Text within images is still challenging; AI often produces garbled or misspelled text. So potentially plan to add text overlays in post-production.

Complex compositions with multiple subjects or specific spatial relationships can be hit-or-miss. 

Brand consistency isn't automatic, even with context, you may need multiple iterations to match your exact brand guidelines. 

Different image generation models support different dimensions, so make sure to understand their limitations.

projectorSlides.title: Itérer et améliorer

projectorSlides.title: Essayer différents modèles

Second, try different models. Image generation models have different qualities to them. 

The best models are constantly evolving, so make sure to follow up on the latest releases and their enhanced capabilities.

Imagine you're a content marketer. You are accountable for the traffic to your company's blog. You know from your company dashboard that traffic has decreased, but you don't know why. Let's uncover the answer with AI.

Before we practice our skills, let's take a step back and understand best practices and risks when working with AI for data analysis.

| Contexte    | Nous avons constaté une baisse dans le tableau de bord et voulons en trouver la cause racine. | Regarde ça.              |

Let's set up our case study. You're a paid media manager at MarketingGPT, a chatbot built specifically for marketing use cases. Your job is to drive user signups using paid social ads on LinkedIn, while keeping cost of acquisition under 10$. 

Now, paid media is all about experimentation. What drives our cost of acquisition down comes from three key areas: audience definition, creative elements like images and copy, and using data to iterate on winning ads. 

We already have campaigns running, but we want to dedicate some budget to an AI-led approach focused only on marketers working in the tech industry.

projectorSlides.title: Étape 1 : Recherche d’audience avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script: First, we'll use AI to ideate and research new audiences, and narrow down our targeting. Be mindful of setting clear goals, context, and limitations. For example, ask for job titles you want to target, relevant countries, industries, and more.

projectorSlides.title: Étape 2 : Générer des variantes créatives
projectorSlides.script:
Next, we use AI to generate fifty different copy variations for our ads. This is content creation at scale. In traditional paid media, we might manually write five to ten variations, but with AI, we can generate fifty unique variations in minutes. 

Here, we'll use the job titles we identify in step 1, and different competitive angles from user interviews, to really hone in on different types of messaging.

projectorSlides.title: Étape 3 : Analyser les performances avec l’IA
projectorSlides.script: Next up, is iteration. After running our campaigns for a week or two, we collect the performance data and use AI for analysis. We'll identify the top performing ads, and which taglines have the most powerful messaging, so we can drive further iteration.

projectorSlides.title: Flux de travail complet propulsé par l’IA
projectorSlides.script: By the end of the capstone, you would have completely re-imagined a paid marketing workflow with AI—from ideation, to execution, and iteration.

projectorSlides.title: Passons à la pratique !
projectorSlides.script: Now, let's get MarketingGPT some customers.

Après avoir terminé votre recherche d’audience, vous êtes prêt à créer des textes publicitaires pour votre campagne LinkedIn. Plus ciblé pour le marketing que des outils prêts à l’emploi comme ChatGPT

projectorSlides.title: Au‑delà des assistants standard
projectorSlides.script:
So far in this course, we've been prompting AI as a general assistant, where for a given task, we provide it clear goals, context, and limitations. 

This can be time consuming if we use AI for the same use-case repeatedly, and can cause misalignment when AI is applied on similar workflows across the same team. 

Custom assistants on the other hand, come pre-configured with instructions, knowledge, and capabilities tailored to a specific task, making them faster, and more consistent on that task.

projectorSlides.title: Assistants personnalisés selon les plateformes IA
projectorSlides.script:
Many AI providers come pre-configured with custom assistants, or let you configure your own. 

The core concept is the same across all platforms: you're creating a version of the base assistant from these systems, and giving it dedicated information or tools so that it's specialized in one task. 

For each provider, they are called differently: In ChatGPT, they're called Custom GPTs. Google's Gemini calls them Gems. Claude uses the term Projects. And in un assistant IA génératif de votre choix, which we'll focus on today, they're called Agents. 

Let's first start with some pre-built custom assistants in un assistant IA génératif de votre choix.

projectorSlides.script:
Before we dive into building, let's understand the key components of any custom assistant. 

Whether in ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or un assistant IA génératif de votre choix, every custom assistant is built on three foundational pillars. 

First, instructions define what your assistant does, its objective, which guidelines to refer to, limitations, and any other context it should be aware of. 

Second, the knowledge base gives your assistant access to relevant data it needs to perform its tasks. These could be the guidelines we want it to stick to, best practices to abide by, or a reference document it should always check. 

Third, capabilities are the tools your assistant can use, like code interpretation, web search, or image generation.

projectorSlides.script:
Throughout this course, you've learned how to accelerate marketing workflows across the entire marketing lifecycle. We started with research, planning, and ideation, then tackled content creation and execution, and finally covered measurement and optimization. 

You now have a comprehensive toolkit for integrating AI into every stage of your marketing work.

| **Création et exécution** | Création et production des supports | Création de contenu de qualité à l’échelle, variantes de textes publicitaires, conception d’assets visuels, adaptation omnicanale...|

| **Itération et passage à l’échelle** | Accent sur ce qui fonctionne et extension aux nouvelles campagnes | Adapter les stratégies à de nouveaux contextes, identifier de nouveaux canaux, affiner les playbooks marketing... |

projectorSlides.title: Un long horizon devant vous
projectorSlides.script:
That said, there's much more that can be done with AI. What we've covered is just the beginning. 

There are many emerging tools and techniques that can assist across a variety of tasks. From workflow automation tools, to vibe coding tools, and more. So make sure to check out other courses to get an even deeper idea on how to drive value with AI in marketing.

projectorSlides.title: Continuez à pratiquer
projectorSlides.script:
For now, the most important thing is to keep practicing what you've learned. The more you use these techniques in your daily work, the more natural and powerful they'll become. 

Try different approaches, experiment with prompts, and find ways to customize AI for your unique marketing challenges. Remember, mastery comes from consistent practice and curiosity.
